question: A safety seat belt in a car exerts a force on our body to:

options.text: facilitate some kind of backward motion
rule out any kind of backward motion

solution:
The correct answer is to__** make **our forward motion slower.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **safety seat belt in a car exerts a force **on our body to make our** forward motion slower**.
 
• When **we travel in a moving car**, our body remains in **a state of rest** with respect to the seat.
 
• But **when the driver applies sudden breaks** or stops the car our **body tends to continue in the same state of motion** because of** its inertia.**
 
• Therefore, **sudden breaks may cause injury** to us by **impact or collision,** and a safety seat belt in a car exerts a force on our body to make our **forward motion slower.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton Law of Motion:**

 
 
• **First Law of Motion:** If a body is at rest remains at rest, or** if a body is moving at a constant speed in a straight line, it remains in motion**.

 
 
• This is known as** the Law of Inertia.**
 
 
 
• **The Second Law of Motion:** States that the **rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the force applied.**
 
• **The Third Law** **of Motion:** States that for **every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.**
